the model says the meaning changed: The hook now runs checks with a private copy built from a different wheel than the plugin's (weakening "per plugin version" and EX-4's "checks that cannot run yet stay silent"), and it newly writes .plumb/session/errors.log into the project, which can conflict with EX-1's "nothing was written into that project".; brought to the owner as a card: The requirement still matches what you asked for: the Claude Code plugin runs plumb's own private copy, kept separately for each user and plugin version, and nothing is written into the project. While that copy isn't ready yet, checks that can't run stay silent.

The latest change to plumb's background-check launcher does two new things:
1. If plumb is reinstalled during a session and the private copy now belongs to a different plumb build, background checks still run on that copy instead of stopping. The mismatch is noted in a log.
2. When a check can't run at all, or fails, it writes a line to a new error log in the project (.plumb/session/errors.log). Before, it said nothing.

The comments in the code show this was deliberate: the goal is that no answer or edit goes unrecorded. But it moves away from two promises in the requirement: one copy per plugin version, and nothing written into the project (EX-1). The prompt from that turn ("Resolve that skill issue too") doesn't clearly ask for this. It's also unclear whether these log lines can appear in a project that hasn't adopted plumb. Because the change looks intentional but isn't clearly requested, you need to decide whether to keep it.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the change, and reword the requirement: when the plugin is reinstalled mid-session, checks may keep using the existing copy, and failures go to a log inside the project's .plumb folder, only in adopted projects") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep the error log but drop the mismatched-copy fallback: checks only ever run on the copy for this plugin version") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Undo both: checks that can't run stay silent and nothing new is written into the project") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (plumb stale card SR-279#3 --consequences "..." --why "...")
